title: How to Pass JustinGuitar Grade 1: Core Targets and Practice Guidelines
summary: In this instructional video, JustinGuitar outlines the practical targets a beginner must meet to pass Grade 1 of the JustinGuitar Beginners Course. The core requirements include tuning with a tuner, memorizing eight basic chords (A, D, E, A minor, D minor, E minor, C, G) and playing them from memory with good tone most of the time; achieving rapid chord changes (30 changes per minute, i.e., about 2 seconds per change); using a steady 80 BPM strumming pattern with a metronome; memorizing five easy songs with simple progressions and performing them for real or via recording; and optional Ear Training Grade 1 and Music Theory Grade 1. The video emphasizes self-assessment, achievable pacing over weeks, and progress-oriented celebration rather than formal external testing. It also encourages recording oneself to reveal and address weaknesses and stresses a forgiving, enjoyable learning mindset.

1-minute chord changes: 30 changes per minute, ~2 seconds per change

Strumming pattern: 'old faithful' at 80 BPM with a metronome
Maintain a consistent strumming pattern while allowing small, controlled variations
Memorize five easy songs with simple progressions
Perform in front of someone or record yourself and post on YouTube for feedback
Recording as a feedback tool to expose and address weaknesses
Optional Ear Training Grade 1 and Music Theory Grade 1 (and related resources)
Practical theory materials available in the Practical Music Theory Course (Grade 1 and 2 are free)
Self-assessment approach: forgiving and realistic progress tracking
General course goal: achieve a sense of achievement and progression through Grade 1
